content: Orlistat is a medication that is prescribed to assist with weight loss when combined with a personalized low-calorie, low-fat diet and an exercise program. It is available in both prescription and nonprescription forms. Additionally, orlistat is used to help prevent weight regain after initial weight loss. This medication belongs to a class of drugs known as lipase inhibitors. It works by inhibiting the absorption of some of the fat consumed in the diet within the intestines. The unabsorbed fat is then excreted from the body through the stool. Orlistat is available in capsule form, both as a prescription and as a nonprescription product, and is taken orally. It is typically taken three times a day with each main meal that contains fat. The medication should be taken during the meal or within one hour after eating. If a meal is skipped or does not contain fat, the corresponding dose of orlistat can also be skipped. It is important to follow the instructions provided on the prescription label or the package label carefully. If there are any aspects of the instructions that are unclear, consult your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Orlistat should be taken exactly as directed, without exceeding or reducing the prescribed dose or frequency. If you are prescribed orlistat, you can request a copy of the manufacturer's patient information from your pharmacist or doctor. For additional details about the nonprescription version, you can visit the website www.MyAlli.com. In some cases, orlistat may be prescribed for uses other than those listed. If you have questions about alternative uses, consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before starting orlistat, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you have any allergies to orlistat or other medications. If you are taking medications that suppress the immune system, such as cyclosporine (Neoral, Sandimmune), discuss this with your doctor. If you are taking cyclosporine, it should be taken two hours before or two hours after orlistat. Provide your doctor and pharmacist with a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking or plan to take.g., warfarin), diabetes medications (e.g. If you have had an organ transplant, cholestasis (a condition where bile flow from the liver is blocked), or malabsorption syndrome (difficulty absorbing nutrients), your doctor will likely advise against taking orlistat. Additionally, inform your doctor if you have a history of eating disorders (e.g., anorexia nervosa, bulimia), diabetes, kidney stones, pancreatitis, gallbladder disease, or thyroid disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, you should not take orlistat. While taking orlistat, adhere to the dietary program recommended by your doctor. Distribute your daily intake of fat, carbohydrates, and protein evenly across three main meals. Consuming a diet high in fat (more than 30% of daily calories from fat) or a single meal very high in fat may increase the likelihood of experiencing side effects. Orlistat reduces the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) and beta-carotene, so it is essential to take a daily multivitamin containing these nutrients. The multivitamin should be taken at least two hours before or two hours after taking orlistat, or at bedtime. If you have questions about multivitamin use, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Avoid foods with more than 30% fat content, and read food labels carefully. When consuming meat, poultry, or fish, limit portions to 2–3 ounces and choose lean cuts. Remove skin from poultry and incorporate more grains, fruits, and vegetables into your meals. Replace whole-milk products with nonfat or low-fat alternatives, and use less fat when cooking. Opt for vegetable oil sprays and low-fat or nonfat versions of salad dressings, baked goods, and processed foods. When dining out, inquire about food preparation methods and request minimal or no added fat. If you miss a dose of orlistat, take it as soon as you remember, provided it is within one hour of eating a main meal. If more than one hour has passed since the meal, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Orlistat may cause side effects, particularly changes in bowel habits, which are most common during the initial weeks of treatment but may persist. Mild side effects include oily spotting on clothing, gas with oily discharge, an urgent need for bowel movements, loose or fatty stools, increased bowel movement frequency, difficulty controlling bowel movements, rectal discomfort, stomach pain, irregular menstrual periods, headaches, and anxiety. If these symptoms are severe or do not resolve, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, though less common, require immediate medical attention. These include hives, rash, itching, difficulty breathing or swallowing, and severe or persistent abdominal pain. If you experience any of these symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store orlistat in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat, moisture, and light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Maintain regular appointments with your doctor while taking orlistat. Engage in a consistent exercise program, but consult your doctor before starting any new physical activity. Do not share your prescription medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Orlistat is marketed under the brand names alli® and Xenical®.
